title: Model catalog contract: discovery API, version-pinning semantics, and profile publication
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a backwards-compatible public contract for model capability discovery and performance profile publication, and formalize version-pinning semantics for hosted/dedicated/private deployments. This ticket defines API shape changes, required metadata for profiles (limits, context window, supported features), and the behavior for pinned vs floating versions when routing requests.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAPI spec updated with /v1/models and /v1/models/{model_id}/profiles endpoints and published to the API portal
API returns per-version capability profiles (max_context_tokens, max_input_tokens, recommended_batching_profile, supported_features list) for both pinned and floating versions
Version pinning header (X-Redwood-Model-Version) semantics documented and honored by router: exact-match pin -> no fallback unless explicit fallback header present
SDKs (js/python) surfaced convenience: model.pin(version) and model.profile() to fetch canonical profile; integration tests exercising SDK calls against mock server
Compatibility fields present for automated fallback: compatible_variants list with min_compatible_version and quantization_compatibility
Profiles can be published as 'performance' variants (latency-optimized, cost-optimized, accuracy-optimized) and clients see recommended_profile key
Migration plan documented for existing customers: 90-day deprecation window for old /models endpoint shape with examples and webhook to notify early adopters
Security review completed and RBAC enforced for profile publication APIs (only model-onboarding role can publish profiles)
notes_and_progress: 2026-01-25: Initial spike completed — compared options: enrich existing /models response vs introduce /profiles subresource. Decided on subresource to avoid payload bloat for list endpoints.
2026-01-28: Draft OpenAPI changes pushed to repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-specs/pull/412). Waiting API review from @Priya Nair and @Diego Alvarez.
2026-02-02: Backend contract agreed: store canonical_profile per model-version and allow additional named profiles (e.g., "latency-optimized", "quantized-8bit").
2026-02-04: Router behavior proposal reviewed in eng-arch; confirmed router uses exact pin semantics unless header X-Redwood-Allow-Fallback=true is present.
2026-02-07: Added fields for automated orchestrator decisions: estimated_tokens_per_second, memory_kv_cache_bytes, gpu_required_tflops.
2026-02-09: Security requested scoped IAM check for publishing endpoints — submitted ticket SEC-1221 (link attached).
2026-02-12: Started SDK changes (js/sdk#220) to expose model.profile() and model.pin() helpers; unit tests scaffolded.
test_plan: Unit tests for OpenAPI validation and backwards-compatibility assertions
Integration test: publish sample profiles for 'gpt-open-7b' v1.2; assert router honors pin header and returns 409 on incompatible pin when strict mode enabled
Load test: profile fetch under catalog request rates (50k qps) to ensure caching layer handles burst
E2E: SDK publish -> backend store -> router routing with fallback header toggles
